posts.author: MarketNotebook
posts.text: Looking for high quality stocks and fno data — Before paying for any dataset, I’d ask for a small sample that includes an expiry day and a few illiquid strikes. That usually exposes missing candles and artificial fills quickly. Also check whether they preserve exchange timestamps, flag gaps instead of silently forward-filling them, and include the original symbol/token mapping for expired contracts. A cheap feed can become expensive if you only discover these problems after building the backtest.
